glossary.DRHP: Draft Red Herring Prospectus, the draft IPO document reviewed before filing.
glossary.SEBI ICDR: SEBI ICDR is the rulebook that tells issuers what an IPO document must disclose.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer checks verify the people and entities named in the draft.
glossary.DIN: Director Identification Number, the unique ID used to verify a company director.
glossary.CIN: Corporate Identity Number, the registration number assigned when the company was incorporated.
glossary.NTA: Net tangible assets means net worth after removing intangible items like goodwill.
glossary.RoNW: Return on Net Worth shows how efficiently the company generates profit from shareholder capital.
glossary.contingent liability: A possible liability that may arise later, depending on how an ongoing matter is decided.
glossary.merchant_banker: The SEBI-authorised intermediary who reviews, diligences, and certifies the draft before filing.

drafts.I: This Draft Red Herring Prospectus relates to a Fresh Issue of equity shares of face value ₹10 each by Satvik Foods Limited, aggregating up to ₹32.00 crore, proposed for listing on the NSE Emerge SME platform. The cover records the issuer’s corporate identity, registered office at Baner, Pune, the price band of ₹104–₹110 per share, a lot size of 1,200 shares, and the appointed intermediaries — Meridian Capital Advisors LLP as Lead Manager, Bigshare Services Private Limited as Registrar, and Anchor Securities Private Limited as Market Maker. The issue is a 100% book-built offer with no offer for sale component.
drafts.II: This section defines the conventions used throughout the document. Company-specific terms ("the Company", "Satvik", "our Promoters"), issue-related terms ("Fresh Issue", "Price Band", "Anchor Investor Portion"), and technical or industry terms ("D2C", "modern trade", "quick commerce") are each given a single meaning. Financial figures are stated in ₹ lakh unless otherwise noted, fiscal years end 31 March, and references to statutes are to those statutes as amended. Abbreviations used in the document — SEBI, ICDR, RoC, DIN, CIN, NTA, RoNW, CAGR — are expanded here on first use.
drafts.III: Prospective investors should consider the following risks together with the rest of this document before investing. Revenue concentration: a substantial share of revenue arises from modern-trade and quick-commerce arrangements, and the loss of a key distribution partner could adversely affect operations. Promoter concentration: post-issue the Promoters will hold approximately 42.7% of paid-up equity, giving them significant influence over shareholder decisions. Regulatory and tax matters: an indirect-tax demand of ₹18.4 lakh is under appeal and, if decided adversely, would create an additional contingent liability. Input-price volatility in millets and edible-oil seeds may compress margins.
drafts.IV: This section carries the general information required for the issue: the registered and corporate office of the Company, the Registrar of Companies with which it is registered, the composition of the Board of Directors, and the details of the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. It records the Lead Manager, legal counsel, statutory auditors, bankers to the issue, the Registrar, and the Market Maker, along with the changes in the Board and in the registered office during the three years preceding this document, and the inter-se allocation of responsibilities between intermediaries.
drafts.V: The Indian packaged-foods market continues to shift toward better-for-you categories, with millet-based products benefitting from public-health messaging and from the policy attention that followed the International Year of Millets. Organised retail penetration, cold-chain expansion and quick-commerce delivery have compressed the distance between small brands and urban consumers. Within this setting, the health-snacking and cold-pressed-oils segments have grown faster than the packaged-foods average, though they remain fragmented, with regional brands competing on sourcing quality and on shelf presence in modern trade.
drafts.VI: Satvik Foods is a Pune-based direct-to-consumer packaged-foods company with a portfolio spanning millet-based snacks, cold-pressed edible oils and ready-to-cook health mixes. The Company operates an asset-light, brand-led model across its own D2C platform, quick-commerce partnerships and more than 4,200 modern-trade outlets in western and southern India, supported by a leased manufacturing facility at Baner, Pune. Revenue has grown at a 49.2% CAGR over FY21–FY23 while EBITDA margin expanded to 14.6%. The Company employs 148 people across manufacturing, supply chain, sales and brand functions.
drafts.VII: The restated summary statements are derived from the audited financial statements for FY21, FY22 and FY23, restated in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations. Revenue from operations grew from ₹2,184 lakh in FY21 to ₹4,863 lakh in FY23, a CAGR of 49.2%. EBITDA rose from ₹262 lakh to ₹712 lakh over the same period, and profit after tax from ₹96 lakh to ₹421 lakh, taking PAT margin to 8.7%. Net worth stood at ₹1,852 lakh and net tangible assets at ₹1,418 lakh as at 31 March 2023, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.29.
drafts.VIII: Pre-issue paid-up equity capital is held as follows: Ananya Deshpande (Promoter, Managing Director) 34.2%; Rohan Kulkarni (Promoter, Whole-time Director) 28.6%; Saama Growth Fund II 18.4%; angel investors (seven holders) 9.2%; the employee stock option pool 6.1%; and other shareholders 3.5%. This section sets out the share-capital history since incorporation in March 2016, including allotments, the bonus issue and the sub-division of face value, the build-up of Promoter shareholding with dates and issue prices, the lock-in position, and the pre- and post-issue shareholding pattern.
drafts.IX: The Fresh Issue is expected to raise ₹32.00 crore, from which issue-related expenses of ₹2.60 crore will be met, leaving net proceeds of ₹29.40 crore. These are proposed to be deployed as follows: ₹13.00 crore toward setting up a new millet-processing line at the Baner facility; ₹9.00 crore toward incremental working-capital requirements; ₹4.50 crore toward brand-building and digital marketing; and ₹2.90 crore toward general corporate purposes. The schedule of deployment runs across FY25 and FY26, with the processing line commissioned in the first year. Deployment will be monitored by the Audit Committee, and any variation in the objects would require shareholder approval in accordance with the Companies Act, 2013.
drafts.X: The price band of ₹104–₹110 per equity share of face value ₹10 has been determined by the Company in consultation with the Lead Manager on the basis of qualitative and quantitative factors. Qualitative factors include the brand position in the millet-foods segment, direct sourcing relationships, and a multi-channel distribution footprint. Quantitative factors include basic earnings per share of ₹6.79 for FY23, return on net worth of 22.7%, and net asset value per share of ₹29.87 as at 31 March 2023, against ₹52.61 on a post-issue basis. At the floor and cap of the band the price-to-earnings ratio works out to 15.3 and 16.2 times FY23 earnings respectively. Comparison with listed peers on P/E, P/B and RoNW is presented alongside, with the peer set and its basis of selection disclosed.
drafts.XI: This section discloses outstanding litigation and regulatory matters involving the Company, its Directors and its Promoters. One indirect-tax matter is outstanding: a demand of ₹18.4 lakh raised in respect of input tax credit availed in FY21, presently under appeal before the Commissioner (Appeals). Management, on the basis of advice received, believes the demand is unlikely to crystallise, and the amount has been disclosed as a contingent liability rather than provided for. No winding-up or insolvency proceedings are pending, no Director stands disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013, and there are no criminal proceedings against the Promoters.
drafts.XII: The Board comprises four Directors: Ananya Deshpande (Managing Director and Promoter, on the Board since 2016), Rohan Kulkarni (Whole-time Director and Promoter, since 2016), S. Iyer (Independent Director, since 2022) and Meera Nair (Independent Director, since 2023). The section sets out each Director’s qualifications, experience, other directorships, terms of appointment and remuneration, together with the corporate-governance framework: the Audit Committee, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, and the Stakeholders Relationship Committee, each constituted in accordance with the Companies Act, 2013 and the applicable listing requirements.
drafts.XIII: The Promoters of the Company are Ananya Deshpande and Rohan Kulkarni, who together hold 62.8% of pre-issue paid-up equity capital. This section discloses their complete profiles — personal details, educational background, business experience, other ventures and directorships — together with the entities forming part of the Promoter Group. It records the Promoters’ interest in the Company beyond their shareholding, the details of related-party transactions during the last three financial years, the common pursuits between the Company and Promoter-Group entities, and the confirmation that the Promoters have not been prohibited from accessing the capital markets.
drafts.XIV: The Declaration records that all relevant provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Government of India and by the Securities and Exchange Board of India established under Section 3 of the SEBI Act, 1992 have been complied with, and that no statement made in this document is contrary to those provisions. It is signed by each Director, by the Chief Financial Officer and by the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, and is countersigned by the Lead Manager as part of its due-diligence certification.
